rule.description: A named Go interface contract is forced on implementors or accepted by consumers while part of its capability set is never used through that contract: required capabilities are never dispatched through the interface, or implementors satisfy dispatched capabilities with pass-through stubs.

checks.description: Detect capabilities that the contract requires of every implementor although no expression ever invokes them through the interface.
checks.detected_relation: interface -> required capability never dispatched through the interface
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The contract obliges every implementor to provide a capability that no consumer of the contract uses, so implementors and consumers depend on behaviour the design does not need.

matches.evidence: slugStage declares IsValidSlug and every pipeline stage is forced to provide it (8 implementors), yet no stage value is ever asked for it; the only real validation calls happen on the concrete noopStage value inside IsSlug and the only dispatch sites are the phase loops of applyStages.

slugStage declares StageName and every pipeline stage overrides or inherits it (8 implementors), but nothing ever asks a stage for its name; the capability is carried for diagnostics that were never built.

checks.description: Detect implementors that satisfy a dispatched capability of the contract only with a pass-through stub that returns its input unchanged.
checks.detected_relation: implementor -> dispatched contract capability implemented as a pass-through stub
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The stage is forced by the contract to carry a capability it does not own; the pass-through body proves the obligation is dead weight for that implementor even though the interface dispatches it.
